text:
Alex K: Heads up — after yesterday's base-image rollout (ubuntu-22.04 + nvidia-container-toolkit 1.12) we're seeing containers fail to find libcuda / libnvidia-ml on ~12% of GPU nodes in us-west1. Logs look like: 
```
Alex K: containerd: starting container: OCI runtime start failed: container_linux.go:xxx: mount callback failed: cannot stat '/var/run/nvidia/driver/nvidia-allocator.sock': no such file or directory
Alex K: error: could not load shared library libcuda.so.1: No such file or directory
```
Priya S: Which fleet subset? Dedicated or shared?
Alex K: Dedicated pool (reserved-gpu-pool-3), rollout happened via image-builder job id: 2026-05-22-0142. Canary passed on 3 nodes but at scale the toolkit hook seems inconsistent.
Dan R: I saw something similar last week when we moved from toolkit 1.9 -> 1.10; the hook path changed and the runtime didn't always mount /usr/lib/nvidia. Could be the install script switched to providing libraries through a different bind mount.
Emily T: Any kernel messages? dmesg or modprobe failing?
Alex K: Kernel modules look fine (nvidia, nvidia_drm), but container runtime fails earlier — before any CUDA call. Sample from kubelet logs: 
```
Alex K: time="2026-05-22T01:55:10Z" level=error msg="failed to setup nvidia mounts: mount failed: exit status 32"
```
Priya S: Can we reproduce with a simple busybox+cuda image? If it's a mount-time race, running the nvidia-container-toolkit hook manually might show it.
Dan R: Agreed. I reproduced locally on an affected node: if the nvidia persistence daemon isn't up when containerd invokes the hook, the toolkit script skips the lib mounts. The change in 1.12 made the check non-blocking.
Alex K: That matches canary behavior — small scale worked because timing was different. At scale, daemon startup is slower due to cloud-init scripts.
Emily T: Workarounds? We can: 1) pin base image to toolkit 1.10, 2) ensure nvidia-persistenced is enabled and systemd start order enforces it, or 3) add a containerd prestart sleep/hook.
Dan R: I pushed a quick patch to image-builder to pin toolkit=1.10 for the Dedicated channel and queued a rollback for the batch rollout.
Alex K: Status update: rollback started for reserved-gpu-pool-3. Ops-bot reports 5/40 nodes remediated so far.
Priya S: Also add a compatibility check in the build pipeline: run a small loop that starts/stops 20 containers in parallel to catch timing issues.
infra-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-045 — nvidia-toolkit-mount-regression, priority=P2, assigned=eng-runtime, link=https://incidents/internal/INC-2026-045
Emily T: Good. After rollback we should schedule a controlled re-release with updated toolkit and a shim that waits for persistence daemon socket before returning success. Dan — can you draft the shim?
Dan R: Will do. I'll open a PR with systemd unit tweak + toolkit shim. Targeting canary on monday morning US hours.
Alex K: Thanks all. Action items: Dan = PR for shim, Priya = add parallel container test to pipeline, Emily = monitor remediation progress & notify customers for Dedicated who reported errors.
Priya S: Adding a note to the postmortem board. :memo:
Alex K: Local repro steps I used (to save time): 
```
Alex K: 1) ssh to affected host
Alex K: 2) stop nvidia-persistenced
Alex K: 3) trigger 100 parallel docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:11.8-base sleep 1
Alex K: 4) observe mount failures in containerd logs
```
Emily T: Thanks — that will help QA. We'll keep this thread updated as rollback completes. :white_check_mark:
